He's easily the physically largest human character. The Brute: His role within the Sons of Garmadon. He's also the largest and physically strongest among them. Co-Dragons: of The Quiet One alongside Mr. E and Ultra Violet. Cool Bike: The Oni Chopper, a massive motorcycle that puts thechopin chopper, with a giant buzzsaw for a front wheel, and has mounted rocket launchers above the driver's seat. It also has a painted on Grundle to boot.

characters.name: Iron Baron
characters.description: An Arm and a Leg: Firstbourne took his left arm and right leg. Asshole Victim: He is an megalomaniacal dragon hunter and abuser, a liar to his own hunters, and also a sexist as poor Faith can attest to.So it's hard to feel bad for him when he's burned into a molten magma statue and doomed to slowly die. Bad People Abuse Animals: He has built his entire society on the exploitation of not only his own people but also dragons, capturing and using them as slaves or at worst killing them for food and decoration. Kai immediately is able to tell he's a bad guy just by simply looking at his throne (and unbeknowst to Kai it's made from the Ultra Dragon's skeleton). Big Bad Ensemble: While the original Ninja are fighting him in the First Realm, Nya, Lloyd, and the Resistance are fighting Emperor Garmadon back in Ninjago. Big Bad Wannabe:His entire goal of finding the Dragon Armor turns out to be pointless, as it was the First Spinjitzu Master's kind nature that allowed him to control the Firstbourne, meaning that he was never going to be able to wield it for his own purposes. He's subsequently defeated in the penultimate episode, as the Ninja return to defeat Garmadon.

characters.name: Heavy Metal
characters.description: The Iron Baron'sNumber Two, a skilled hunter and warrior carrying the Dragon Blade.Her true name is actually Faith and hides her gender through a conical hat and a mask. She eventually turns over to help the Ninja after overhearing that Wu is the first Spinjitsu Master's son. Action Girl: They're one of the Iron Baron's most skilled hunters, easily dealing with the Ninja after revealing their powers in the arena, granted their Dragon blade also helped.And she becomes an essential ally to the Ninja, especially as they fight off the other hunters. Back for the Finale: They sit out most of Season 10 due to barely being able to escapethe First Realm with her life but gets back up in the final episode to help the Ninja in defending the Monastery. Broken Pedestal: A loyal follower of the Iron Baron and hisNumber Two,but being forced to keep her gender hidden and then finding out that he completely lied about the Oni has her completely lose all respect for him, even if she did pull aHeel–Face Turnbefore the Oni revelation. The Dragon: The second-in-command of the Dragon Huntersuntil she defects from Iron Baron. She takes over leadership once the Iron Baron is dealth with.

characters.name: Daddy No Legs
characters.description: A hunter who uses mechanical spider legs to walk since he has no lower half. Half the Man He Used to Be: Has no lower half, needing to use mechanical spider legs to move around. Punny Name: He's a spider-themed villain whocan't walk on his own. Spider People: Has mechanical spider legs.

characters.name: Jet Jack
characters.description: The only obviously female hunter who uses a jet pack to fly. The Dragon: AfterHeavy Metal/Faithturns against Iron Baron, Jet Jack becomes the new second in command of the Dragon Hunters. Lady Looks Like a Dude: She has a very unfeminine appearance which could make one easily mistake her for a man. The Smurfette Principle: The only female Dragon Hunterwho is obviously a woman, as it is later revealed that Heavy Metal was alsoa woman the whole time.

characters.name: Muzzle
characters.description: A hunter who can only speak in grunts due to his muzzle. Evil Wears Black: He sports black and is a villain. Intelligible Unintelligible: He's this to the viewers, though the other hunters can understand him perfectly.

characters.name: Arkade
characters.description: A hunter who has a slot machine built into his body. Body Horror: Has a whole slot machine built into his body. Whatever incident led to him having that mustn't have been pleasant. Cyborg: Is probably more of one than any other hunter, considering he has a slot machine embedded in his torso. The Faceless: We never actually get to see what's underneath his welding mask. Probably for the best. Noodle Incident: How and why he has a slot machine in his body, we may never know...

characters.name: Chew Toy
characters.description: The hype man of The Pit. Butt-Monkey:It's in his name. Slab, the dragon in the Pit, has presumably used him as a chew toy many times judging by how many injuries he has on his body. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: He's not exactly all there, granted you'd have to be crazy to let yourself become a living chew toy for a massive dragon.

characters.name: The Omega
characters.description: Arc Villain: Is the main villain of Season 10: March of the Oni. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: Well, more like "evil cannot comprehend lesser evil", but he doesn't understand why Garmadon would try to protect Ninjago from the Oni instead of joining them. Evil Sounds Deep: His voice is extremely deep. Generic Doomsday Villain: The Omega is the main villain of Season 10, but gets very little characterization beyond his desire to wipe out all of reality, and mostly serves as a way to show that as bad as Garmadon has become, he hasn't completely given up on his humanity. Hate Sink:Definitely. Every time the Omega is onscreen, he is shown to be arrogant and ruthless, and he has no qualms in taunting Garmadon over his insecurities and wiping out all of existence.

characters.name: Ice Emperor
characters.description: Amnesiac Hero:Thanks to Vex interrupting his diagnostic of the mech, he loses all memories of who he was. Arc Villain:The Heavyof the Ice Chapter of Season 11. Back for the Finale:This persona resurfaces in Zane during the aptly named Season 15 episode, Return of the Ice Emperor. Criminal Amnesiac:He is actually Zane, wiped of all his memories and lied to by General Vex that he is the Ice Emperor. The Emperor: The Ice Emperor ruled Never-Realm for decades.

characters.name: Blizzard Samurai
characters.description: The frozen soldiers of the Ice Emperor. Everything's Better with Samurai: Samurai that are both powered and even made of ice at that. Golem: While some are corrupted humans, others are made entirely out of ice. Literally Shattered Lives: Due to some being essentially ice golems, if they take enough damage or are defeated they immediately shatter into pieces. Was Once a Man: Some are actually human soldiers corrupted into Blizzard Warriors byZane's use of the Scroll of Forbidden Spinjitzu.

characters.name: Grimfax
characters.description: A high-ranking officer of the Blizzard Samurai. He used to be the king of the Never-Realm until he was overthrown. Anti-Villain: He's not actually evil, but he is forced into doing Vex and the Ice Emperor's bidding with no other option except death. When he hears from Lloyd that the Ice Emperor used to be a good person, Grimfax releases him and Kataru from their prison cells so they can help him take back his kingdom. Barbaric Battle Axe: His weapon of choice is a massive double-bladed battle axe and while anAnti-Villain, he's also a powerful foe and enforcer for the Ice Emperor when theNinjafirst meet him. Even using his battle axe to extinguish the Ice Fishers' sacred fire after they won the battle. Forced into Evil: He was given two choices: either serve the Ice Emperor or die by his hand. The Good King: He was a benevolent ruler of the Never-Realm and never sought to attack anyone or commit any other kind of misdeed until Vex andan amnesiac Zanecame along and usurped him.

characters.name: Unagami
characters.description: A.I.-cronym: Unagami:UnfinishedAdventureGame1. Anti-Villain:He isn't truly evil, just a hurt and confused A.I. lashing out at his creator for shutting him down. Arc Villain: The ruler of Prime Empire in Season 12 and the main antagonist of the season overall. The Bad Guy Wins:He achieves his goals of creating a portal to Ninjago and confronting his creator Milton Dyer. Blue-and-Orange Morality:Since he is an A.I., and a young one at that, he genuinely doesn't get why trapping someone in a digital world just to give them a more intense gaming experience is wrong. He didn't even see the point in explaining to Milton what happened to Scott in over 30 years, simply because he knows that little about human morality.

characters.name: Avatar Harumi
characters.description: Back from the Dead: She seems to be Harumi back from the dead, however, it is revealed that she isn't the real Harumi, only a digital copy of her. Impostor-Exposing Test: Lloyd figures out this Harumi is a fake when she is unable to give the answer to what they did on the first night they were alone (ACall-Backto the events of the Season 8 episode "The Jade Princess"). Impostor Forgot One Detail: She's identical to the real Harumi in appearance and personality, but lacks her memories. Makeup Is Evil: Her facial appearance is based on Harumi's stint as the Quiet One, where she wore black lipstick and red face paint. Shout-Out: Her outfit resembles that of the one worn by The Bride inKill Bill.

characters.name: Red Visors
characters.description: Troopers that serve Unagami. Heel–Face Turn: Thanks to Unagami having his own, the Red Visors simply stop terrorizing Ninjago and go back to Prime Empire. However "Crystalized" has them being one of the many armies that choose to help fight the Crystal King and his own army. Implacable Man: They can show up just about anywhere in the game and can be difficult to fight in large groups. Red Eyes, Take Warning: Their visors are red, as their name implies. Zerg Rush: Their favored tactic is swarming targets in large groups and overwhelm them with massive amount of laser fire until they run out of lives.

characters.name: Ritchie
characters.description: A member of the Whack Rats, anthropomorphicNPCrats who work for Unagami, he was sent alongside other rats to ambush the Ninja in the Forest of Discontent. I'll Never Tell You What I'm Telling You!: Tells the Ninja this way that he was ordered by Unagami to ambush them. Molotov Cocktail: Seemingly a common weapon amongst Whack Rats. When taking part of the Speedway Five-Billion, he attacks other racers with one. Usually throwing them directly into the cockpit/driver's seat. One-Way Visor: He and many other whack rats sport cybernetic glowing red visors that are attached to their heads. Fitting with the videogame cyberpunk-aesthetic of Prime Empire. You Dirty Rat!: Tries to ambush the Ninja and later lures them into a trap located inside a glitch.

characters.name: Skull of Hazza D'ur
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: It's not made clear if it's an artifact used by Hazza D'ur or D'ur himself reincarnated, although the latter is heavily implied. Dragon-in-Chief: Downplayed; the Skull gives the Skull Sorcerer all of his power, although given it's just a skull it can't really do much on its own. Repeated for Emphasis: It tends to repeat or emphasize whatever the Skull Sorcerer says. The Ninja make fun of that habit.

characters.name: Grief-Bringer
characters.description: A dragon that terrorized the Munce and Geckles until it was slain by Lily, brought back as an undead by the Skull Sorcerer. Dracolich: Became one thanks to the Skull Sorcerer and the Skull of Hazza D'ur. The Dreaded: To both Munce and Gecklesare they fear him. Evil Is Burning Hot: It's a villain with alight green fire. Technicolor Fire: Its fire is light green.

characters.name: Re-Awakened
characters.description: The Re-Awakened, also known as the Awakened Warriors or the Dark Skeletons, are undead skeleton warriors created using the Skull of Hazza D'ur. They are not Skulkin despite the similarities. Ambiguous Situation: In the flashback scenes of "Crashing Together" fromDragons Rising, two Re-Awakened skeletons are seen attempting to kidnap children to make them work on an unknown mining operation. It's never revealed if this is Vangelis is up to his old tricks again or they are doing their own independent yet still illegal and immoral mining operation. Decapitated Army:Once Cole destroys the Skull of Hazza D'ur with Spinjitzu Burst. This causes almost all of them to crumble back into piles of bones. However "Magma Mayhem" a comic from the Ninjago Magazine revealed that some survived and continued to be loyal to Vangelis. No-Sell: They use special vengestone weapons that render the Ninjas' element powers useless. Low-Tech Spears: Compared to the more properly made weapons used by the Ninja, Munce and Geckes. The Re-Awakened make use of primtive spears with shafts made of long bones and crude spearheads fashioned from vengestone.

characters.name: Mammatus
characters.description: The leader of the Keepers. Big Bad Ensemble: While Mammatus isn't evil, and is being tricked into offering gifts to the fake Wojira (Ronin), his overprotectiveness of the Amulet makes him the most immediate threat ofThe Island. Good All Along: He and the Keepers turn out to not be evil, and help the Ninja after they clear up the misunderstanding. The Heavy: The most prominent threat ofThe Island. My God, What Have I Done?: He quickly becomes remorseful when the Ninja call him out for turning Jay into aHuman Sacrifice.

characters.name: PoulErik
characters.description: A two-headed Keeper who serves as Mammatus's second-in-command. The Dragon: Is the second-in-command of the Keepers. Multiple Head Case: A case where one head is located on top of the other. It's said that the two heads do not always get along with each other.

characters.name: Prince Kalmaar
characters.description: Antagonistic Offspring: He is the son of King Trimaar and secretly went behind his father's back to sink vessels and cause destruction for his own purposes.He promptly kills his father the moment he feels that he no longer needs his old man alive. Arc Villain: The main villain of Seabound/Season 14. Asshole Victim: Let's just say, the audience is gonna be cheeringonce he getsEaten Aliveby the Wojira. Bait the Dog: In the past, he pretended to care for Benthomaar, simply to get his adoptive brother to do what he wanted him to. Cain and Abel: The Cain to Benthomaar's Abel, being a villainous and treacherous monster who wanted to start a war for the sake of his ego in contrast to his open-minded and kind brother.

characters.name: Gripe
characters.description: Kalmaar's manservant and his second-in-command. Co-Dragons: Seems to be this with Glutinous — while the spider-legged scientist works on awakening Wojira, he commands Meropia's army. Even Evil Has Standards: While he has no qualms about working for someone who is plotting to destroy the surface world, he objects to firing at the Ninja while they are in Merlopia, as Merlopian civilians could get killed. Palette Swap: He is distinguished from the other Maaray Guards by having green highlights in place of the others' cyan. Secret-Keeper: He, unlike other Merlopians, is well aware thatKalmaar killed his father, but, keepingUndying Loyaltyto his master, never reveals it.

characters.name: Glutinous
characters.description: Co-Dragons: With Gripe. Half the Man He Used to Be: The lower part of his body is completely mechanical. Heel–Face Turn: After Kalmaarfinally reawakens Wojira. He decides to warn the Ninja of the impending invasion. It seems to stick as he actually fights alongside the Maaray Guard against the Crystal King's army in "Crystalized", My God, What Have I Done?: WhenWojira finally awakens, he believes he may have made some "poor career choices" and rushes to warn the Ninja. Of course, this could've simply been him realizing that his bossdoesn't need him anymore. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: He's essentially the Merlopian equivalent to both Char and Clancee, as he is an nervous underling working for a harsher antagonist just like the previous two. Although he bears more similiarites with Clancee, as they both haveArtificial Limbs, while Clancee has aSea Dog Peg Leg, Glutinous is riding a spider walker (similar to the one used by Cyrus Borg).Both eventually turn on their bosses after seeing just how far they were willing to go for power, However unlike Clancee, Glutinous is far more fortunate.

characters.name: Wojira
characters.description: An ancient storm spirit that took the form of a giant sea serpent and terrorized early Ninjago using the Storm and Wave Amulets until she was defeated by Nyad and sealed away in a temple located in the Tartarus Trench. Kalmaar seeks to reawaken Wojira and use her power to destroy Ninjago. Blow You Away: She has the elemental power of Wind. Which allows her to create giant storms. Eldritch Abomination: A huge, ancient entity that was around long before the First Spinjitzu Master came to Ninjago, wielding the forces of water and wind using the Wave and Storm Amulets. Greater-Scope Villain: The overarching villain ofThe IslandandSeabound. She's also the villainess the First Spinjitzu Master and Nyad had to defeat in order to free the World of Ninjago from a great danger and to use her amulets in order create both Ninjago Island and the Dark Island. Knight of Cerebus: Things get really serious when Wojira is finally reawakened, exercising her power to subjugate Ninjago to a violent storm that puts everyone in danger.

characters.name: Captain Soto
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: His arch-rival pirate is Nadakhan the Djinn. Ascended Extra: He's a one-shot villain in Season 2, primarily to justifya fight between pirates and ninjas, but becomes an ally to Jay in Season 6 due to both having a shared enemy in Nadakhan.However due to Season 6's events being undone by Jay's last wish, he returns to being a minor character. Back from the Dead: Brought back by Garmadon using the Megaweapon. Boxed Crook: Winds up in the same prison as Pythor, as shown in Season 4. Cool Ship: His pirate ship was the Destiny's Bounty.

characters.name: Fenwick
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Was completely forgotten after the end of Season 5but returns in the "could-be-canon" web novel "The Splinter in the Blind Man's Eye", as the enigmatic "Wishmaster". Dirty Coward: He values his own life above everyone else's and resorts to trickery to deal with his enemies. The moment things go south for him, he flees in a panic. Facial Horror:Nimbus dida numberon him as most of his face had been ripped open to the point that hisskullwas visibile. Hate Sink: There's nothing good about him,and it gets even worse in "The Splinter in the Blind Man's Eye" which has him rewrite someone's destiny to have them get killed andeatenby Nimbus. It's All About Me: His own life is all that matters to him, not even caring about the devastation Morro will unleash on Ninjago.

characters.name: Fugi-Dove
characters.description: A wannabe supervillain in a bird costume who makes frequent appearances starting with Season 11. Animal Lover: Can be seen feeding and caring for birds in Ninjago City when he's not in the middle of any "crimes". Butt-Monkey:No oneis aware of who he is, with P.I.X.A.L. stating he has no criminal record and doesn't even remember him when his brother mentions her putting him in jail. The Cameo: Was initially one of the many characters missing after the Merge, but he makes a cameo in the season 2 episode "The Blood Moon" ofNinjago: Dragons Rising. Catchphrase: "My cry fills the night!"

characters.name: Miss Demeanor
characters.description: A flamethrower-wielding criminal who appears in Season 14, having been hired by an unknown employer to smuggle Vengestone across the Ninjago countryside. Berserk Button: It's not Missus Demeanor, it'sMissDemeanor. Dub Name Change: Due to the troubles with translating herPunny Name, some dubs (like French and Russian) changed her name to "Miss Dynamite". Evil Counterpart: To Kai and to a lesser extent, Skylor.In Kai's case, they both weaponize fire.In Skylor's case, they are bothAction Girl's who mimic Kai's fire attacks. In Skylor's case, it's through Amber while in Miss Demeanor's case, it's through her flamethrowers. In Kai's case, they both weaponize fire.

characters.name: The Great Devourer
characters.description: According to a legend, once all five Serpentine tribes unite, they will be able to find the four Silver Fang Blades and unleash the "Great Devourer". The Fang Blades are said to enhance the Devourer's abilities and make her unstoppable, releasing a terrible evil that will turn day into night. According to Sensei Wu, she will keep growing as long as she consumes. She is responsible for Garmadon's villainy, as she bit him when he was a child, corrupting him with her evil. The Devourer slept under the Lost City of Ouroboros until Pythor put the Fang Blades into the statue of her and she rose out from underneath the city. She was destroyed by Lord Garmadon with the power of the Golden Weapons of Spinjitzu. All Your Powers Combined: All of the Great Devourer's abilities, attacks, and traits appear to bebeefed-up versions of the main five Serpentine tribe's abilities. She can burrow across vast distances like the Constrictai, can swallow entire buildings whole à la thenear-extinctAnacondrai, even a single drop of her venom can turn people evil or bring inanimate objects to life (similar to the Hypobrai's mind control and the Fangpyre's ability to infect and zombify others into fellow Fangpyre or various Snake/X chimeras), and her skin color and venom greatly resemble that of the Venomari. Animalistic Abomination: A giant snake that causes destruction wherever she goes. Attack Its Weak Point: Has one on the top of her head.Garmadon kills her by diving off the top of a building with all four Golden Weapons and attacking this weak point.

characters.name: Skales
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: After becoming the Snake King, he leads the other Serpentine in an attempt to bury Ninjago City underground. However, he ends up releasing the Stone Army, and his forces are easily defeated by them. The Dragon: First to Slithraa, beforebetraying and usurping himand later to Pythor during the latter's tenure as the King of all Serpentine. Dragon Ascendant: He planned on becoming the new leader of the Serpentine after Pythor was eaten by the Great Devourer, but Lord Garmadon wins their trust before he does and leaves him with only the other Generals. The Good King:He ends up becoming this after having a family, leading the Serpentine to a more peaceful future. Heel–Face Turn: In the later episodes,after getting a wife and a kid. He cements this byhelping the people of Ninjago take shelter during the attack of the Golden Master and later by assisting them in fighting against the Fake Anacondrai army.

characters.name: Slithraa
characters.description: Brought Down to Normal: His fate after losing the Slither Pit duel with Skales. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Hasn't physically appeared since the Season 3 finale. Dragon-in-Chief: To Lloyd when he had control of the Hypnobrai, as the only reason he had any authority among them was because Slithraa was the General. When Skales defeats him and takes his place as leader, Slithraa loses all authority over the Hypnobrai and Lloyd is banished. Hoist by His Own Petard: He attempts to hypnotize Lloyd, but due to the latter's clumsiness, he falls over and causes Slithraa to hypnotize himself after staring at his reflection on an ice wall.Lloyd:No. I will controlyoufrom now on. Out of Focus: After Skales takes his place as leader, Slithraa begins appearing less frequently. "The Titanium Ninja" is the last episode he appears in before disappearing entirely.

characters.name: Pythor P. Chumsworth
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: One of Lloyd's most personal foes, in fact he even tries to have a go at killing him several times after Season 3 and is even content with banishing his father to the Cursed Realm. Arc Villain: While the five tribe leaders were on even footing at first, he eventually manipulated his way into this role in Season 1. Asshole Victim: After he's eaten by the Great Devourer and presumed dead, none, not even Skales, mourns him, which is fitting considering he was the one who released it without thinking of the consequences. Back for the Finale: He returns after 6 years of absence in Season 15,Crystalizedas part of the Council of the Crystal King. The Bad Guy Wins: An interesting case. He succeeds in unsealing the Great Devourer and causing mayhem as he had intended, but gets eaten by her soon after, though survives this fate. He still technically succeeded in his goal, even if the Devourer was ultimately killed in the end.

characters.name: Strike
characters.description: Defector from Decadence: She grew disillusioned with her species as a whole when they only united to wage war on humanity and the Elemental Masters despite her wishing peace and for all to unite against the prophecy of the Golden Master, leading to her siding with the Masters and helping them stop and imprison the others. The Smurfette Principle: The first female Anacondrai. Sole Survivor: Alongside Pythor, though unlike him she wasn't sealed away after the end of the Serpentine War. There Is Another: Pythor for many years was shown to be the only survivor of his tribe, theStrike of the Serpentinegraphic novel reveals Strike's existence and her survival by switching sides in the Serpentine Wars; though her current whereabouts are unknown. What Happened to the Mouse?: Her current fate outside of not being sealed with the rest of the Serpentine is unknown.

characters.name: Acidicus
characters.description: The general of the Venomari. After hisHeel–Face Turnhe serves as a Serpentine Elder and historian. All There in the Manual: Acidicus's name was not mentioned during season one to season ten, only appearing in other media such as the toys. This only gets averted at last when in season eleven Acidicus' name is finally mentioned by Skales. Hidden Depths:Season 3 shows that he has an extensive knowledge of Serpentine legends and acts as a sort of knowledge keeper who can be relied on for informing others of the fact.Season 11 reveals that Acidicus likes books and even became a librarian offscreen. Season 3 shows that he has an extensive knowledge of Serpentine legends and acts as a sort of knowledge keeper who can be relied on for informing others of the fact. Season 11 reveals that Acidicus likes books and even became a librarian offscreen.

characters.name: Supreme Commander Machia
characters.description: The Supreme Commander of the Vermillion warriors. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: She called her fellow commanders out for disobeying her orders, losing Wu upon dealing with Lloyd, andeating sliderswhile attempting to watch over the rapidly aging prisoner. Co-Dragons: She shares the position of second in command of the Vermillion warriors with the other two Vermillion commanders Raggmunk and Blunck. Until Krux and Acronix promote her to Supreme Commander, giving her command over the other commanders. Creepy Cute: Acronix sure thinks so. The Dragon: Since she's the most competent out of the three commanders, she's essentially this to Krux and Acronix.

characters.name: Commander Raggmunk and Commander Blunck
characters.description: The Commanders of the Vermillion warriors. Co-Dragons: They share the position of second in command of the Vermillion Warriors with Machia until Machia is promoted to Supreme Commander. Hive Mind: Can control the other Vermillion Warriors in this way. My Instincts Are Showing: They hiss at each other after getting into an argument. Number Two for Brains: They hold the position of commander, but neither of them are exactly the sharpest tools in the shed.

characters.name: Aspheera
characters.description: Leader of the Pyro Vipers, a Hypnobrai sorceress. The first Serpentine that knows Spinjitzu. Arch-Enemy: A mutual example with Sensei Wu. Aspheera seeks revenge on Wu for supposedly betraying her to the point it becomes her primary motivation. Wu, in turn, detests her for using him and Spinjitzu in her bid for power, which leads him to distrust the Serpentine for many years and gave rise to his motto to "Never trust a Snake". Aspheera is to date the one enemy that Wu shows the most animosity to, even after the Serpentine had aHeel–Race Turnand made peace with Ninjago, being the most reluctant to seek her help to save Nya and being completely distrustful of her when she arrives at the temple. Arc Villain: She's the primary villain of the Fire Chapter of Season 11. Back for the Finale: Returns in Season 15,Crystalizedas part of the Council of the Crystal King. Catchphrase: "Revenge! Revenge!"

characters.name: Char
characters.description: Ambiguously Related: He has some similarities to the Constrictai, with his black scales. Whether he is one is not stated. The Dragon: Serves this role to Aspheera. Professional Butt-Kisser: Pretty much everything he says and does is him trying to win Aspheera's favor. Red and Black and Evil All Over: A villain with both red and black. What Happened to the Mouse?: The last time we saw him he was fleeing the battlefield. Whatever happened to him afterAspheera's defeatis anyone's guess.According toWord of God, Char ended up returning to death alongside the rest of the reanimated Pyro Vipers after Aspheera was stripped of her fire powers.

characters.name: Giant Stone Warrior
characters.description: A giant Stone Warrior and the first among the Stone Army to be reawakened by the Great Devourer's venom. The Ninja face it in a museum, and unable to overpower it, lure it into a sinkhole. Giant Mook: It is larger than the normal troops within the Stone Army, serving as the biggest among them. Multi-Armed and Dangerous: He has 4 arms like General Kozu and is part of aNigh-Invulnerablearmy. So Last Season: Goes from a dreadedGiant Mookamong the Overlord'sDoom Troopsthat the Ninja struggle to fight initially to a minor inmate that can be kept in prison and easily overpowered by the Ninja. Sole Survivor: The Stone Army aredestroyed by Lloyd after he unlocks his Golden Power, but the Giant Stone Warrior seen in Kryptarium Prison ends up being theLast of His Kind, likely because he wasn't caught in the blast.

characters.name: Min-Droid
characters.description: A Nindroid who was made smaller than the others due to the factory he was made in running out of metal. Berserk Button: Hates having his size being made fun of. Butt-Monkey: Is constantly made fun of for his appearance and suffers a lot of abuse from Cryptor. The Dog Bites Back: Finally stands up to Cryptor in "The Titanium Ninja" after overhearing the general belittling him and starts beating him up. Foil: Min-Droid interestingly serves as a contrast to the Giant Stone Warrior. They are both minions created to serve the Overlord and get more screentime in comparison to the other nameless mooks in their respective army, but Min-Droid and the Giant Stone Warrior serve as aMini-MookandGiant Mookrespectively. The Giant Stone Warrior was initially feared in his debut due to his invulnerability, while Min-Droid was treated as aButt-Monkeyby the other Nindroids. The Giant Stone Warrior ends up being theLast of His Kinddue to the other Stone Warriors biting the dust when Lloyd first defeats the Overlord, whereas Min-Droid dies alongside Cryptor when Zane defeats the Overlord, with the nameless Nindroids outliving them.

characters.name: Mister F
characters.description: An upgraded model of Mr. E, and a general in the Crystal King's army. Ambiguous Situation: Pythor describes Mr. F as the latest model of Mr. E. However, it's unclear if this meant that he's Mr. E rebuilt, an entirely new nindroid but with Mr. E's memories, or if he is a new nindroid made from completely separate ties from Mr. E. Back from the Dead: He's a new model based on the original Mr. E. Katana Superiority: It's not Mr. E. - or rather Mister F. - if he doesn't have one of his katanas. Red Eyes, Take Warning: He still has red eyes and he's even more dangerous than before.

characters.name: Vengestone Army
characters.description: Also called the Crystal Army, they are an army created by Kabuki Mask, specifically designed to overpower Ninjago's populace and counteract the Ninja's powers. Man of Kryptonite: They're made of Vengestone, whichnegatethe Ninja's Elemental Powers. PIXAL has to upgrade the Ninja's vehicles for them to be able to destroy them. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Barring their ability to convert people into more of them, they're an implacable army made of a type of mineral that the Ninja struggle to fight against, similar to the Stone Army. Given that the Overlord created both, it's likely not a coincidence. Technically Living Zombie: They can add more to their ranks by simply touching the denizens of Ninjago, whose bodies turn purple andhave crystal shards jutting out of them.

characters.name: Shapeshifting Monsters
characters.description: Bluff the Impostor: One of the shapeshifters impersonates Sensei Wu, but Zane, Jay, and Cole realize their Sensei is a fake when Cole asks if he wants a cup of tea. The real Sensei Wu would of course agree; the shapeshifter who took his place claims to hate tea. Master of Disguise: The shapeshifters can mimic anyone from the memories of those they encounter. No Name Given: The species is so old that its name has been lost to history. Rage Against the Reflection: No mirror-smashing here, but seeing their own reflections is the shapeshifters' one weakness. Sealed Evil in a Can: One of the important functions of the Skeleton Army was to keep these monsters from escaping the Underworld and entering Ninjago. Then Lord Garmadon sent the Skeleton Army to attack Ninjago instead. Oops.

characters.name: Master Yang
characters.description: The creator of Airjitzu. In a bid for immortality, he accidentally turned himself into a spirit, with all of those who wished to be his students similarly being turned into ghosts trapped within his temple. Be Careful What You Wish For: Twofold. His attempts to become immortal in form and memory result in both his ghostly imprisonment and being erroneously remembered as a martial arts master who failed to get even a single student to train at his temple before he vanished. Big Bad: Of theDay of the Departedspecial. Heel–Face Turn: Has one when Cole reminds him that he would remembered forever as the creator of Airjitzu. Heroic Sacrifice: When Cole and Yang try to make it to the Rift, but find it impossible. Yang decides to settle his debts and throws a confused Cole into the Rift, sacrificing his chance at becoming human again.

characters.name: First Spinjitzu Master
characters.description: As the name suggests, he was the first person to ever master Spinjitzu, which he used to create the realm of Ninjago with the Golden Weapons, where he fathered two sons, Wu and Garmadon, before disappearing to another realm. All Your Powers Combined:Inverted. He was actually the original user of all theElemental Powers, having split them with the Elemental Masters. The Faceless: Any time he puts in a physical appearance, his face is obscured, either because his back's to the camera, or because of the shadow of his hat. Theonlytime his face is seen is in theSpinjitzu Brothersbooks, and a blink-and-you'll-miss-it moment in "Day of the Departed". Greater-Scope Paragon: He was the first person to master Spinjitzu and created the realm of Ninjago as well as the Golden Weapons. Hybrid Power: Season 8 reveals that he's a hybrid of dragon (beings with the power of creation) and oni (beings with the power of destruction), and he's FAR more powerful than either.

characters.name: Cliff Gordon
characters.description: An actor famous for theStarfarerfranchise andJay's biological father. Action Hero: Or at least played one on TV. Big Fancy House: He owned a large villa that Jayinherited thanks to Nadakhan granting him his first wish. Catchphrase: Fear isn't a word where I come from! Disappeared Dad:Before Nadakhan granted his first wish, Jay didn't even know Cliff was his real father.

characters.name: Clutch Powers
characters.description: A famous explorer known for his many past exploits. Adaptational Jerkass: This version of Clutch Powers is a lot more arrogant, selfish, lazy and less adventurous than his original series counterpart, only exploring the discovered pyramid in Season 11 when the Explorers Club threatens to cancel his membership because he hadn't done any exploring in over a decade. He gets worse inseason 14 as he tries to commit outright plunder by stealing the Amulet from the Keepers and leaving only a counterfeit. Canon Foreigner: He originates fromLEGO: The Adventures of Clutch Powers. Catchphrase: Whenever he finds himself in trouble he always says: "Gumdrops!" Dirty Coward: Chose to run and hide rather than help the ninja deal with Aspheera. He does so again when Kalmaar shows up, which especially stands out when the other members of the Explorers Club are more than willing to help fight them off.

characters.name: Ulysses Trustable
characters.description: The new Mayor of Ninjago City who came into office after Nya merged with the Endless Sea. He opposes the Ninja as being too destructive and supports the New Ninja. Dirty Coward:As soon as his treasured New Ninja get crystalized by the villains, he leaves the scene (and the series) by running for his life, forgetting about the rest of the city. Fun with Acronyms: His full name is Ulysses Norville Trustable, which when shortened comes out asUNTrustable. Ironic Name: His sunrame is "Trustable" whenhe's anything but. Hate Sink: While he has a point in refusing the Ninja's request to let them release Aspheera, he's such a jerk that it's easy to root for the Ninja.He also turns out to be a coward who will quickly abandon any pretense of wanting to help the city in favor of saving his own skin once the New Ninja end up failing to stop the Crystal King's invasion. In fact, pretty much the only reason for his existence is for the Ninja to remain sympathetic even after they become criminals.

characters.name: Robot Manager/Coffee Bot
characters.description: Ambiguously Related: Ronin mentions that he owns both Steeper Wisdomandthe robot manager’s coffee shop. It’s unknown if this also means he built the Coffee Bot as well. Cheaters Never Prosper: In “Zaney Chess Game”, she manages to beat Zane in a game of chess but when she outstretched her arm to get her tea, Zane's queen fell out of her sleeve, meaning that she took said Queen under Zane’s nose without playing fair and square.She was eventually thrown out of Steeper Wisdom for cheating. Connected All Along: In “The Taste Test”, Ronin mentions he owns both Wu's Steeper Wisdom and the robot manager’s coffee shop. This means she is associated with the former. Defeat Means Friendship: Upon besting Wu in sales, the latter decides to make a truce with her, thus putting the two shop owners on good terms. Mysterious Past: We know nothing of her origins, such as where she came from or who her creator is (assuming it’s not Ronin).
